# head_instantiation_paren_prettier_divergence

An `{#each}` head, or a shorthand `{#await}` head, that ends on an instantiation expression's closing `>` and was written in a paren pair: prettier-plugin-svelte strips the pair, and tsv keeps it.

tsv: `{#each (f<T>) as item}`, `{#await (c ? a : f<T>) then v}`, `{#await (f()<T>) catch e}`
Prettier: `{#each f<T> as item}`, `{#await c ? a : f<T> then v}`, `{#await f()<T> catch e}`

## Reason

**Semantic preservation (`as`, `then`).** Svelte's parser hands the head to acorn-typescript, which reads a type argument list only where the token after its `>` cannot start an expression on the same line. The `{#each}` block's `as` and a shorthand `{#await}` block's `then` are words, which can, so bare, the head is the comparison `f < T > as` and does not parse (`expected_token`); prettier's own next pass throws on its output. It is the head-keyword twin of the `as` / `satisfies` rule inside an expression ([instantiation_paren_assertion_follow](../../../typescript/typescript_specific/generics/instantiation_paren_assertion_follow_prettier_divergence/)), and the axis is again what the head PRINTS last, not its node: a prefix operator's argument (`-f<T>`), a binary's right operand (`a * f<T>`, `a ?? f<T>`), an angle-bracket assertion's operand (`<U>f<T>`), a conditional's alternate, an arrow's expression body, an `await` argument and the last operand of a same-operator logical chain — nested to the right included (`a ?? (b ?? f<T>)`, which prints rebalanced as `a ?? b ?? f<T>`) — all end on the close, so the pair wraps the whole head — and a pair written around the instantiation alone, or around a chain's right-nested tail, moves out to it (`unformatted_ours_inner_pair`). A block head adds no pair of its own, so every one of those kinds reaches it bare, unlike the left of `as`, which pairs them by kind.

**tsv's own parser (`catch`).** `catch` does not continue a comparison for acorn-typescript, so Svelte reads `{#await f()<T> catch e}` — prettier's form — as the same tree as the paren form, and that output is correct for Svelte. tsv's own parser refuses a bare instantiation ahead of `catch` (a tsv over-rejection), so tsv keeps the pair there to keep its own output reparseable; the `catch` cells record that choice rather than a prettier bug.

Where the head's own `}` or a `,` follows — a full-form `{#await}`, a `{#key}`, an `{#each}` with no `as` — nothing is joined to the close, and the pair strips in both formatters (Svelte rejects a paren-led `{#each (…)}` with no `as`).

Three spellings are not cells. An `await` head (`{#each (await f<T>) as item}`) keeps its pair like the rest, but `svelte compile` refuses a template `await` without `experimental.async`, which leaves the variant's render check no oracle, so it is pinned in [`tests/instantiation_follow_parens.rs`](../../../../instantiation_follow_parens.rs). The value-less shorthand `{#await (f<T>) then}` strips in prettier to `{#await f<T> then}`, which parses — as the comparison `f < T > then`, a block with no `then` section — so it is no tsv fixed point, which `authoring:audit` requires of `output_prettier.*`; it is pinned in the same Rust test. And an inner pair around a conditional's alternate (`{#each c ? a : (f<T>) as item}`) cannot be a variant: prettier prints that head from Svelte's unwound offsets and loses the `)` (`{#each c ? a : (f<T> as item}`, the [ts_head_paren_tail](../each/ts_head_paren_tail_svelte_prettier_divergence/) bug), so it lands on no documented form; the same Rust test pins it.

See [conformance_prettier.md](../../../../../docs/conformance_prettier.md) §Prettier bug index and [conformance_prettier_svelte.md §Svelte: block-head instantiation before a head keyword](../../../../../docs/conformance_prettier_svelte.md#svelte-block-head-instantiation-before-a-head-keyword).
